name: a-gaslamp-silent-film-still
prompt: A single frame pulled from a reel of 1919 silent horror cinema, portrait format: night in a city park, an iron-and-slat bench under one gas lamp whose glass lantern hangs directly overhead, its flame the only light in the world. On the bench sits a stout, wealthy gentleman in a tall silk top hat, frock coat stretched across a round belly, watch chain across the waistcoat; the lamp drops straight down on him, so the hat brim cuts his face in half: above the cheekbones only two hollow black pits where his eyes should be, with one tiny pinprick of reflected flame in the left one, and below it a powdered, plaster-white face and a wide courteous smile whose teeth catch the light while his lips print almost black. He lifts one gloved hand lazily from the wrist, fingers drooping, dismissing the man beside him. That man is a young soldier home from the war, thin, in a rumpled army greatcoat, one trouser leg folded and pinned below the knee, a wooden crutch laid across his lap; he sits at the edge of the lamp's circle, so he is mostly a dark shape, only his knuckles on the crutch and the line of one cheek touched by light. Camera at seated eye height, a steady medium two-shot, both figures in the lower half of the frame. Above the lantern, the upper third is soft unbroken blackness. Shot on early blue-sensitive orthochromatic nitrate stock through an uncoated lens with a hand-cranked camera: blown whites and inky blacks with almost nothing in between, no smooth gradients, coarse dancing silver grain, vertical scratches and dust flecks on the emulsion, slight gate softness at the edges and a round iris vignette closing in from the corners. Monochrome only, no modern lighting, no digital polish, no text or lettering anywhere in the frame. Thanks.
